newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia to benefit from US sugar quota - QSC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia to benefit from US sugar quota - QSC.

text.p: The Queensland Sugar Corp (QSC) on Wednesday welcomed the United States Department of Agriculture's (USDA) announcement of a revised 1996/97 raw sugar quota programme which sees a minimum import quota of 1.70 million tonnes with provisions for increases during the year.
For the first time, three automatic increases of 200,000 tonnes can be made if additional raw sugar needs to be imported to maintain adequate supplies in the United States, QSC said in a statement.
QSC chief executive David Rutledge said the revised programme would enable exports of Australian raw sugar to increase.

Although the quota of 1.70 million tonnes is lower than the initial proposal of 1.88 million tonnes, if the increases go ahead total imports could reach 2.30 million tonnes, more than 1995/96 U.S. sugar imports of 2.0 million tonnes, he said.
QSC also welcomed the increased flexibility the USDA had announced in administration of the quota, he said.
The Queensland industry would now be able to better match its supply of raw sugar with its U.S. customer requirements, he said.
If Australia's previous 8.3 percent share of overall quota allocations was maintained, its share of the new allocation would be about 140,000 tonnes, excluding any share of increases during the year.

Australia exported 165,000 tonnes of raw sugar to the U.S. during the 1995/96 quota period, up from 123,000 tonnes the year before as a result of the additional imports required during the year, he said.
QSC owns almost all of Australia's annual sugar crop.
